name: Prophetic Fulfillment

objectives.text: Identify that God knows the future and tells his people what will happen
Name Bethlehem as the town where God promised long before that Jesus would be born
Retell God's first promise of a Savior in the garden and explain how Jesus kept that promise
Match the promise of a virgin-born child in Isaiah to its fulfillment in the birth of Jesus
Explain the biblical test of a true prophet, that his word from the Lord always comes to pass
Summarize the Old Testament prophecies of the crucifixion and match each detail to its Gospel account
Explain how Jesus fulfilled the Passover as the Lamb of God
Compare vague predictions such as horoscopes with specific biblical prophecies such as the naming of Cyrus
Explain how Jesus taught that the Law, the Prophets, and the Psalms point to his suffering and resurrection
Explain from Scripture why God's past fulfillment of prophecy gives grounds for trusting his unfulfilled promises such as Christ's return
Explain how Jesus fulfilled Moses' promise of a coming prophet like him
Construct a chart of major Messianic prophecies with their New Testament fulfillment citations
Distinguish direct predictive prophecy from typological fulfillment using New Testament examples
Analyze the probability argument that one man fulfilling many specific Messianic prophecies is beyond chance, and identify its strengths and limits
Interpret Daniel's vision of the statue and the succession of empires in light of later history
Analyze Ezekiel's prophecy against Tyre in relation to the historical record of its destruction
Analyze the Suffering Servant passage and evaluate the claim that the Servant is the nation of Israel rather than the Messiah
Analyze Daniel's seventy weeks prophecy and compare the main interpretations of its timing for the Messiah
Evaluate the objection that Jesus deliberately arranged his life to fulfill prophecy by identifying prophecies outside human control
Evaluate the objection that biblical prophecies were written after the events they describe
Evaluate the objection that New Testament writers misused Old Testament texts by examining how they cite prophecy in context
Construct a reasoned argument for the divine origin of Scripture from predictive prophecy
Evaluate the role of the argument from prophecy within the Reformed teaching that full persuasion of Scripture's authority comes from the inward work of the Holy Spirit

changes: Kept and reworded real competencies (God knows the future, Bethlehem, crucifixion prophecies, Passover, vague versus specific prediction, probability, Daniel 2, Tyre, typology, prophecy chart, maneuvering objection, divine origin argument) and moved several to grades where they fit better. Dropped vague filler (Jesus did everything God promised, only God can tell the future 100% of the time) and recast the future-promises objective as knowledge rather than personal application. Dropped the synthesis with miracles since that belongs to the sibling sub-topic Miracles as Proof. Added Genesis 3:15, Isaiah 7:14, the test of a true prophet, Jesus' own reading of the Old Testament, the prophet like Moses, Daniel's seventy weeks, the Suffering Servant identity question, the after-the-fact and misuse objections, and the Reformed view of evidence and the Spirit's witness. Replaced whole-chapter references with verse ranges and added confession anchors where they state the doctrine.
